evidence.why: Shows branch ordering, sector-boundary subtraction, conditional offset/FAT advancement, next-read arguments and terminal cleanup.
Initializes card->buffer from dst and advances it by 0x200 for each successful segment before invoking the higher-level callback.

facts.rationale: Corrects unconditional-looking state advancement and exact-byte-accounting implications while documenting the verified cross-file destination-pointer lifetime.
facts.value: ReadCallback selects __CARDBlock[chan]. Incoming errors terminate before file-state accounting; otherwise card->fileInfo supplies the operation state, and a preexisting negative length signals cancellation. It subtracts the distance from the current offset to the next sector boundary from fileInfo->length. If the remainder is nonpositive, it completes without advancing offset or iBlock; this subtraction can leave a negative remainder after a successful final partial-sector read. Only when data remains does it advance offset, follow fat[iBlock], validate the successor, and issue __CARDRead at sectorSize * iBlock for min(remaining length, sectorSize) bytes into card->buffer. That destination pointer was initialized and advanced by the low-level read implementation in CARDRdwr.c. Terminal handling captures and clears apiCallback, releases the control block with the final result, and invokes the captured callback with chan and result.

evidence.why: Complete seek, starter and continuation data flow, including early terminal branches.
Destination state is maintained by the lower transfer layer.

facts.rationale: Replaces the incorrect claim that every completion updates length, offset and block before either continuation or release, preserving the overall pipeline explanation.
facts.value: CARDFileInfo supplies the channel, directory-entry index, cached logical offset and allocation block. __CARDSeek acquires control, checks the requested extent, stores the file pointer and requested length, and positions through directory/FAT metadata. CARDReadAsync checks access, invalidates the full destination range, stores the API callback, and converts the positioned block plus in-sector offset into the first bounded physical read. CARDRdwr.c maintains the advancing destination pointer reused by subsequent reads. On a non-error, non-canceled callback, ReadCallback subtracts the distance to the next sector boundary; only a positive remainder causes logical-offset and FAT-block advancement and another read. Exhaustion leaves the last transfer's starting offset/block unchanged and may leave a negative length for a partial-sector finish. Callback termination clears and invokes the saved API callback after releasing control; startup failures instead return directly.

evidence.why: Seek assertions, explicit guards, acquired-control cleanup and success retention.
Distinguishes callback termination from startup errors and shows cancellation/accounting order.
Interrupt-protected cancellation predicate, sentinel assignment and return statuses.

facts.rationale: Separates immediate-return failures from callback terminal cleanup and preserves the distinct meanings of negative length before and after accounting, including the cancellation producer.
facts.value: The read pipeline reserves channel control while positioning and performing asynchronous transfers. Explicit cached-position, extent, FAT, alignment and access guards return CARD errors; some input validity requirements are assertions only. Seek/access failures release acquired control as shown, while successful initiation leaves completion to ReadCallback. An immediate __CARDRead startup error releases control and returns without clearing or invoking apiCallback in CARDReadAsync. Within ReadCallback, an incoming negative result wins over cancellation; otherwise a negative stored length becomes CANCELED. Sector-boundary subtraction then causes either normal exhaustion or FAT advancement and another transfer. A negative residual produced by that subtraction can represent successful partial-sector exhaustion, not cancellation. All terminal paths inside ReadCallback capture and clear apiCallback, release control, and invoke the captured callback once. CARDCancel disables interrupts around its test: an unattached card returns NOCARD; a busy channel with the identical stored file pointer gets length = -1 and returns CANCELED; other cases return READY. It restores interrupts and leaves an active transfer to report cancellation through its later callback.
